title: Cohomology f-maps between exact module rows respect their connecting maps
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $E:0\to E_1\xrightarrow{u}E_2\xrightarrow{v}E_3\to0$ and $F:0\to F_1\xrightarrow{u'}F_2\xrightarrow{v'}F_3\to0$ be short exact sequences [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] of Zariski $\mathcal O_Y$-modules and $\mathcal O_X$-modules respectively [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose $\phi_j:E_j\to f_*F_j$ are $\mathcal O_Y$-linear coefficient maps, with $f_*u'\circ\phi_1=\phi_2\circ u$ and $f_*v'\circ\phi_2=\phi_3\circ v$. Use the canonical maps $T_f^q(\phi_j):H^q(Y,E_j)\to H^q(X,F_j)$ induced by $f$-maps [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], and right-derived global-section cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology]. If $\delta_E^q:H^q(Y,E_3)\to H^{q+1}(Y,E_1)$ and $\delta_F^q:H^q(X,F_3)\to H^{q+1}(X,F_1)$ are the canonical connecting maps of these long exact sequences, then for every $q\geq0$ one has $$T_f^{q+1}(\phi_1)\circ\delta_E^q=\delta_F^q\circ T_f^q(\phi_3).$$ The equality uses the $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-module structures, with scalars on the target restricted along $f^\sharp$. No flatness of $f$ and no quasi-coherence or acyclicity of the six modules is required. In particular it applies to the adjunction-unit coefficient maps for a flat pullback, and to compatible coefficient maps over an automorphism.

source.place: Tag 01F9 (equation-functorial-derived) and section-cohomology-sheaves (equation-cohomology-modules); Tag 05TE (lemma-right-derived-delta-functor). Compatibility of the specified f-map with the two boundary maps is an agent-written consequence of these resolution constructions, not a verbatim assertion of either tag.

proof.text: Choose compatible injective resolutions $F_j\to I_j^\bullet$ of $F$ and $E_j\to J_j^\bullet$ of $E$, zero in negative degrees, with degreewise split short exact rows $I_1\to I_2\to I_3$ and $J_1\to J_2\to J_3$. These exist by the scheme-module enough-injectives theorem and the object horseshoe lemma. Put $A_j=f_*I_j$ termwise. Its row is still split exact: applying the additive functor $f_*$ to the inclusion, projection and splitting identities preserves those identities. The section rows of $I$ and $J$ are likewise split exact. No assertion that $f_*$ preserves arbitrary exact sequences or injectives is needed.

source.place: Tag 013T (lemma-injective-resolution-ses), objects in degree zero; cohomology.tex Tag 01FB (remark-explain-arrow)

proof.text: Write $s_j:E_j[0]\to J_j$ for the augmentations and $a_j:E_j[0]\to A_j$ for $E_j\xrightarrow{\phi_j}f_*F_j\to f_*I_j$. The two coefficient squares and the horseshoe augmentation squares say precisely that $(a_j)$ is a morphism of rows. In each degree form $Q_j=\operatorname{Coker}((s_j,-a_j):E_j[0]\to J_j\oplus A_j)$, with differential induced from the direct sum. These differentials exist because $(s_j,-a_j)$ is a cochain map. Its components are monomorphisms since $s_j$ is monomorphic. Apply the snake lemma to the map of short exact rows $E[0]\to J\oplus A$ in each degree: its three kernels vanish, so the three cokernels $Q_1\to Q_2\to Q_3$ form a short exact row, including both endpoint zeros. Denote the canonical cochain maps by $b_j:J_j\to Q_j$ and $t_j:A_j\to Q_j$; the quotient relation gives $b_js_j=t_ja_j$. Both families are morphisms of rows.

source.place: Tag 010H (lemma-snake), applied degreewise to graph maps; agent-written simultaneous pushout of the resolution diagrams of cohomology.tex Remark 01FB

proof.text: Put $C_j=\operatorname{Coker}(s_j:E_j[0]\to J_j)$ as a complex. Since $s_j$ is an injective resolution, it is a quasi-isomorphism; the long exact sequence for $0\to E_j[0]\to J_j\to C_j\to0$ gives $H^n(C_j)=0$ for all $n$. The pushout short-exact-sequence lemma, applied degreewise to $0\to E_j[0]^n\to J_j^n\to C_j^n\to0$ along $a_j^n$, identifies its pushout with the displayed quotient $Q_j^n$ and gives $0\to A_j\xrightarrow{t_j}Q_j\to C_j\to0$. Its long exact sequence now gives that every $t_j$ is a quasi-isomorphism. All these complexes vanish below degree zero.

source.place: Tag 013T (lemma-injective-resolution-ses), proof Step 1 pushout comparison; Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain)

proof.text: Apply the complex horseshoe lemma to the short exact nonnegative row $Q_1\to Q_2\to Q_3$. It gives a short exact row $K_1\to K_2\to K_3$ of nonnegative complexes of injectives and a row morphism $r_j:Q_j\to K_j$ of quasi-isomorphisms. Set $\lambda_j=r_jt_j:A_j\to K_j$ and $\beta_j=r_jb_j:J_j\to K_j$. Then $\lambda_j$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $\beta_js_j=\lambda_ja_j$, the precise augmentation equation required for the $f$-map construction. The $K$ row splits in each degree: injectivity of $K_1^n$ extends its identity over the monomorphism $K_1^n\to K_2^n$, giving a retraction. Thus its section row is split exact. By the pushforward-injectives sections theorem, $\Gamma(Y,\lambda_j):\Gamma(X,I_j)\to\Gamma(Y,K_j)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, despite the possible failure of $f_*I_j$ to be a complex of injectives.

Write $\partial_J,\partial_I,\partial_K$ for the homology boundaries of the three split exact section rows. The canonical resolution identifications $\iota_{J_j}^q:H^q(Y,E_j)\simeq H^q\Gamma(Y,J_j)$ and $\iota_{I_j}^q:H^q(X,F_j)\simeq H^q\Gamma(X,I_j)$ identify the canonical module-cohomology boundaries with $\partial_J$ and $\partial_I$. Here the canonical boundary is that of Tag 05TE: $H^q$ of $R\Gamma$ applied to the boundary of the distinguished triangle of $0\to E_1[0]\to E_2[0]\to E_3[0]\to0$, read through the single-object identifications. To check this identification, apply the fixed horseshoe derived-triangle comparison to $v=\Gamma(Y,-)$ and $v=\Gamma(X,-)$, which are additive and left exact by the global-sections theorem. Its image-row hypotheses hold because the rows split, and extension by zero remains exact, including degree zero. The endpoint homology equations in that comparison, together with the nonnegative-complex derived-boundary comparison, turn the third square of its triangle morphism into $\iota_{J_1}^{q+1}\delta_E^q=\partial_J^q\iota_{J_3}^q$ and $\iota_{I_1}^{q+1}\delta_F^q=\partial_I^q\iota_{I_3}^q$. This checks the boundary convention rather than assuming the horseshoe and triangle constructions agree.

source.place: Tag 05TE (lemma-right-derived-delta-functor), via the fixed horseshoe comparison; Tags 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain), 014Q (definition-distinguished-triangle), 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor)

proof.text: For either section-row morphism $m=\Gamma\beta$ from $\Gamma J$ to $\Gamma K$, or $m=\Gamma\lambda$ from $\Gamma I$ to $\Gamma K$, the split-boundary formula proves the required square directly. A cocycle $z$ in the third complex has a lift $w$ in the middle complex. There is a unique $x$ in the first complex with $i(x)=dw$; it is a cocycle since $i(dx)=d^2w=0$ and $i$ is injective. The boundary is $[x]$. The element $m_2(w)$ lifts $m_3(z)$ and $d(m_2w)=m_2(dw)=i_K(m_1x)$, so the target boundary is $[m_1x]$. Hence $\partial_K^qH^q(\Gamma\beta_3)=H^{q+1}(\Gamma\beta_1)\partial_J^q$ and $\partial_K^qH^q(\Gamma\lambda_3)=H^{q+1}(\Gamma\lambda_1)\partial_I^q$. The split-boundary formula allows this choice of lift: replacing a chosen split lift by $w$ adds $i(y)$, changing $x$ by $dy$, hence not its class.

source.place: Tags 011J (lemma-ses-termwise-split-cochain) and 011K (lemma-ses-termwise-split-long-cochain); lift calculation for the two row morphisms

proof.text: Set $B_j^q=H^q(\Gamma\beta_j)$ and $L_j^q=H^q(\Gamma\lambda_j)$; each $L_j^q$ is invertible by Step 4. The choices in Step 4 satisfy every clause of the defining $f$-map resolution diagram. Independence of those choices therefore gives $T_f^q(\phi_j)=(\iota_{I_j}^q)^{-1}(L_j^q)^{-1}B_j^q\iota_{J_j}^q$. From Step 6, multiply the $\lambda$ identity by inverses and then use the $\beta$ identity to get $$\partial_I^q(L_3^q)^{-1}B_3^q=(L_1^{q+1})^{-1}\partial_K^qB_3^q=(L_1^{q+1})^{-1}B_1^{q+1}\partial_J^q.$$ Substitute the two identities of Step 5 and cancel the resolution identifications. This is exactly $\delta_F^qT_f^q(\phi_3)=T_f^{q+1}(\phi_1)\delta_E^q$.

source.place: Tags 01F9 (equation-functorial-derived), 01FA (equation-functorial), 01FB (remark-explain-arrow); agent-written cancellation of the two boundary squares

proof.text: The equality is also an equality of $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-linear maps: each $T_f^q(\phi_j)$ has the linear lift with target scalars restricted along $f^\sharp$ given by the basic-linearity theorem, and the connecting maps are module-linear, as is also evident from their section-complex boundary formula. Restriction of scalars changes no underlying elements, so the equality just proved is the same equality between these linear maps. The construction used only the hypotheses displayed in the statement, for every $q\geq0$. A flat pullback gives an exact sequence $f^*E$ whenever that specialization is made, and naturality of its adjunction unit supplies the two required coefficient squares; for an automorphism any compatible coefficient maps meet the same hypotheses. These are therefore instances of the equality already proved.
